cards.explanation: The answer is Moses. The LORD says to Joshua, “…as I instructed you through Moses…” Moses was Israel's leader, so these instructions were already on the books. I hear a thing once and call it done, then lose it before the cookies cool, friends.

The answer is someone who kills another by accident. God says these cities are so that “…anyone who kills another unintentionally or accidentally may flee there.” That's who the refuge is for, friends. An accident is no small thing, and God made a place for it.

The answer is elders. The one who flees “…states his case before its elders…” Then the elders bring him into the city and give him a place to live among them. They're the ones listening at the gate, friends.

The answer is False. Here's what God says: the elders “…are to bring him into the city and give him a place to live among them.” Nobody sends him out to camp by the wall, friends. He gets a place inside, among them.

The answer is True. God says, “…they must not surrender the manslayer into his hand…” The text gives the reason, friends: that man killed his neighbor accidentally without prior malice. So even if the avenger of blood pursues him, the answer is no.

The answer is until his trial and the high priest's death. God says, “He is to stay in that city until he stands trial before the assembly and until the death of the high priest serving at that time.” That's two markers, bakers, and the text gives both. I'd love to tell you how many days that adds up to, but the verse doesn't say.

The answer is back to his own home. God says, “Then the manslayer may return to his own home in the city from which he fled.” After the high priest serving at that time dies, home is open to him, friends. I think that front door would look mighty good.

The answer is beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho. The text says, “And beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho, they designated Bezer…” Ramoth and Golan are over there too, friends. So there are three cities on that side and three on the other.

The answer is the Israelites and the foreigners among them. The verse says, “These are the cities appointed for all the Israelites and foreigners among them…” Both are named, bakers, and the reason is “…so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there…” The unintentional part matters, and the verse keeps it right there.
